# Intake Brief — End of game stats (MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV)

## Problem statement

The Main Street **Game Over** overlay currently presents only a *static*
end-of-run snapshot (per-player rows, score breakdown, challenges). Players
cannot see **how their economy evolved turn by turn**, so they cannot tell what
worked and what did not, or learn from a failed run. This item adds per-turn
history tracking to the game state and a **third column of end-of-game
graphs** (profit per turn, cash, businesses, staff and reputation at end of
turn), with the **cash-at-end-of-turn** figure surfaced on the Summary column
and a link to the detailed stats.

## Users

- **Main Street player at game over** — wants a visual run recap instead of
  just a final number.
  - *As a player, I want to see my cash, reputation, businesses and staff
    change turn by turn, so I can understand what worked and improve my next
    run.*
- **Competitive player** — wants the same trajectory for their own seat, so a
  loss against AI can be diagnosed.
- **Balance team / designers** — benefit from a deterministic, serialisable
  per-turn series they can inspect (and reuse for analytics).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn — `{ turn, coins, reputation, score, profit,
   businesses, staff }` — where `profit` is the turn's net coin delta
   (reusing the existing `weekStartCoins` snapshot). The snapshot is recorded
   on **both** the deferred (`deferResourceApplication`) and legacy end-of-turn
   paths, and is never recorded twice for the same turn.
2. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState` and restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`;
   legacy saves without the field load with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data).
3. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing
   composed graphs for: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of turn**,
   **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn**, and **reputation
   at end of turn**.
4. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final
   **Cash at end of turn** figure, and provides a link/affordance to the
   detailed stats column.
5. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive mode and fits the 1280×720 viewport without text clipping or
   vertical overflow; the existing Game State and Summary content is retained.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established conventions:
   Phaser-free pure model for series data, `hudContainer` parenting, depths
   199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (interactive), everything pushed into
   `overlayObjects`; the overlay reads committed state only (no mutation),
   adds no animation (reduced-motion safe) and returns early in
   `scene.replayMode`.
7. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture (both paths, no
   double-record), serialise/deserialise round-trip and legacy fallback, and
   the pure series model; browser tests assert the third column and the cash
   line render in both modes.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer decisions (see Appendix):**
  - Target project is **`tce-main-street`** (the item was mis-filed in the
    ContextHub worklog; relocated as this item).
  - **Per-turn history = Option A.** The save game does **not** hold a full
    per-turn history — only the current-turn `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score`
    snapshot — so a new per-turn series must be added, **reusing the existing
    snapshot mechanism/pattern** (persisted alongside the save, legacy
    fallback).
  - **Charting = external charting library** (producer Q3 = B; e.g. Chart.js),
    not hand-rolled Phaser Graphics (A) or SVG-as-texture (C).
  - **No additional stats** beyond the five listed (producer Q4 = "No").
  - **Layout = add a third column** to the Game Over overlay (producer Q5),
    rather than a separate full-page stats screen.
- Game engine is **Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`**; overlay rendering lives in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`.
- External chart library integration with the Phaser canvas must not regress
  headless/Monte-Carlo runs or replay mode (chart module is skipped there).
- CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD
  pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- **Game Over overlay:** `showGameOverOverlay()` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — two columns (**Game State** /
  **Summary**) with a top band (title + end-reason headline) and the
  Play Again / Menu controls anchored at the panel bottom (panel is 900 px
  wide, laid out by `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap`). The pure, Phaser-free
  content model is `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`
  (`buildGameOverPlayerRows`, `buildGameOverChallengeSummary`,
  `formatEndReason`).
- **Current-turn snapshot:** `state.weekStartCoins` / `weekStartRep` /
  `weekStartScore` are set in `executeWeekStart`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`) and serialised in
  `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The per-turn net row
  (`appendTurnNetRow`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) derives the
  turn's deltas from that snapshot and logs
  `Turn <n> net: <deltas> (score: <delta>)`.
- **Ledger history:** `EconomyLedger.getHistory()`
  (`core/src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, imported as
  `@rule-engine/EconomyLedger`) records *every mutation*, is **not
  serialised**, and is **not per-turn** — unsuitable as-is for the graphs.
- **Counts available at turn end:** businesses = non-null entries in
  `state.streetGrid`; staff = `state.staffCards.length`; cash/reputation =
  `state.resourceBank`; score = `state.finalScore`.
- **Precedent:** the Monte Carlo harness already captures a per-turn series
  (`economyHistory: [{ turn, coins, reputation, score }]`) in
  `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` for balance analytics — a useful shape to
  mirror.
- **Save/load:** `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState`
  in `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, with legacy fallbacks for absent
  fields.

## Desired change

1. **State.** Add a `TurnStatSnapshot` interface (`turn`, `coins`,
   `reputation`, `score`, `profit`, `businesses`, `staff`) and
   `turnStatsHistory: TurnStatSnapshot[]` to `MainStreetState`; initialise it
   to `[]` in `setupMainStreetGame` / `createCompetitiveState`.
2. **Capture.** Record one snapshot at the end of each completed turn —
   covering the **deferred** path (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, after deltas
   are applied) and the **legacy** path — so the turn's net profit is computed
   against `weekStartCoins` exactly like `appendTurnNetRow`. Guard against
   double-recording when the two paths overlap (e.g. keyed by `turn`).
3. **Persistence.** Serialise `turnStatsHistory`; on load, default to `[]`
   for legacy saves.
4. **Model.** Extend `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` with a pure
   series builder (e.g. `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)`) returning the five
   requested series plus the final "cash at end of turn" value.
5. **Render.** Add a **third column** to `showGameOverOverlay()` rendering the
   graphs via the chosen external charting library (encapsulated in a small
   helper module so the model stays Phaser-free and testable), and add the
   **Cash at end of turn** line plus a link to the stats column on the Summary
   column. Recompute `panelW` / column widths / `panelH` so all three columns
   fit the 1280×720 viewport.
6. **Guardrails.** Skip chart construction in `scene.replayMode` / headless
   mode; keep the pure model testable without booting Phaser or the chart
   library.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory`
  to `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — Initialise `turnStatsHistory: []` for
  single-player and competitive setups.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Record the per-turn snapshot on both
  closing paths (reuse the `weekStartCoins`/`appendTurnNetRow` pattern).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — Serialise/restore `turnStatsHistory`
  with a legacy `[]` fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — New pure series builder
  (`buildGameOverStatSeries`) + final cash-at-end-of-turn value.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Third column rendering + Summary
  cash line + link; widen/rebalance the panel layout.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **New** thin wrapper around the
  external charting library (skipped in replay/headless).
- `package.json` — Add the charting-library dependency.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats.test.ts` — **New** unit tests (capture,
  round-trip, legacy fallback, series model).
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` /
  `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts` — Third-column and cash-line
  assertions.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` / `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` —
  Document per-turn history and the end-of-game stats column.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed) — the
  epic that built the current Game Over overlay.
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed) — the
  layout this item extends to a third column.
- **MS-0MUWE6MA30038RGY** – Game-over summary test harness (completed) — the
  fixture/helper pattern to reuse for tests.
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – Credit AI challenge completions to the AI seat
  (completed) — introduced the per-seat Game Over breakdown.
- **MS-0MUNB4ZXQ0081EX7** – Storyline coverage analytics in Monte Carlo
  harness (open) — consumes a per-turn economy series, the same shape this
  item persists.
- **Related docs:** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Activity Log —
  Effective Deltas and Per-Turn Net, § Win conditions),
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.
- Automated find-related report appended below (if produced).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — external chart library vs Phaser canvas.** Chart.js needs a canvas
  context; overlaying it on the Phaser canvas and keeping it out of
  headless/replay runs needs care. *Mitigation:* isolate the library behind
  `MainStreetStatsChart.ts`, lazy-load/skip in replay/headless, verify bundle
  size.
- **Risk — deferred vs legacy capture paths** could double-record or miss the
  final turn. *Mitigation:* record keyed by `turn` in the shared closing tail,
  with targeted unit tests for both paths.
- **Risk — save/load compatibility.** *Mitigation:* legacy fallback to `[]`,
  with a round-trip + legacy test.
- **Risk — three-column overflow at 1280×720.** *Mitigation:* recompute panel
  width/height and add a browser fit assertion.
- **Assumption — competitive-mode series scope.** In single-player the five
  series describe the run's economy. In competitive mode the shared
  `resourceBank` is seat-scoped during a turn; this brief assumes the graphs
  show the **human seat's** trajectory. *Open question, recorded in the
  Appendix* — the producer may instead want every seat as a separate series.
- **Assumption — "link to a more detailed screen" is satisfied by the third
  column**, per producer Q5; no separate scene is added.
- **Scope-creep risk:** additional stats or chart types beyond the five listed
  (producer Q4 = none) must be raised as separate work items, not folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Correct project?** This item was created in ContextHub (the Worklog
  CLI tool) but describes a Main Street game screen.
  - **Answer (producer): `tce-main-street`.** Source: interactive reply,
    2026-10-16. *Action:* item relocated — created as MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV in
    `tce-main-street`; the mis-filed WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02 was closed as a
    relocated duplicate.

- **Q2 — Per-turn history tracking.** The save holds only the current-turn
  `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score` snapshot; a full per-turn history must be added
  unless the save already carries one.
  - (A) Add per-turn history tracking, reusing the snapshot mechanism.
    **Recommended.**
  - (B) Use only static current values (no historical graphs).
  - **Answer (producer):** "Doesn't the save game have that snapshot? If not A
    otherwise reuse that mechanism." *Research:* inspected
    `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — the save persists only the **current**
    `weekStart*` snapshot, not a per-turn series; the `EconomyLedger` history
    is per-mutation and not serialised. Therefore **Option A** applies, reusing
    the `weekStart*` snapshot pattern and persisting a new series. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q3 — Chart/graph approach.**
  - (A) Phaser-based line/bar charts (custom `Graphics`). **Recommended** at
    the time of asking (no new dependency).
  - (B) External charting library (e.g. Chart.js).
  - (C) SVG line plots rendered as Phaser textures.
  - **Answer (producer): B** — use an external charting library (overrode the
    recommendation). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q4 — Additional stats?** Beyond profit/turn, businesses, cash, staff and
  reputation at end of turn.
  - **Answer (producer): No.** Only the five listed stats. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q5 — Summary-screen placement / detailed screen.** "Place the cash at end
  of turn on the summary screen and add a link to a more detailed screen" — is
  the Summary column the right place, with a button to a full-page graph view?
  - **Answer (producer): Add a third column.** The detailed graphs live in a
    third column of the Game Over overlay rather than a separate screen.
    Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope).** In competitive mode,
  should the graphs plot (i) only the human seat's trajectory, or (ii) every
  seat as a separate series? *Working assumption: (i) human seat only.* Noted
  for producer confirmation during review; not blocking.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed)
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1** – Game-mode selector UI (completed)

- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, action, add, added (+311 more)

# Enter-to-end-turn browser wait exceeds the 60 s hook above ~2x CPU oversubscription

## Headline

The `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait in
`tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` is already at the largest
budget the 60 s browser hook permits (40 000 ms = 16 000 ms cap + 24 000 ms
margin + 20 000 ms boot = 60 000 ms), yet it fails at ≈2× CPU oversubscription
because the bounded end-of-turn deferral is re-polled on Phaser's clamped game
clock, so the forced day start is detected late. **Decision: make the
deferral's safety cap starvation-proof** — one extracted helper whose deadline
and re-poll run on wall clock, enforced even while the page is not painting
(producer, Q1 = C, Q2 = 1).

## Problem statement

The soak evidence on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L shows the gate passes 20/20 quiet
(peak load 15.3), passes 2/2 at 8 burners (peak 23.6), and fails exactly one
wait — `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` — at load ≥ ≈31
(≈2× oversubscription, 16 burners, peak 32.8). That wait's budget is already at
the ceiling the 60 s hook permits, so no poll-budget tweak inside the hook can
rescue it.

Root cause (mechanism, verified against the installed `phaser` source):
Phaser's `TimeStep` clamps the per-frame delta it feeds scenes — under
`smoothStep` (default on) each frame contributes at most `1000/fps.min`
(200 ms) — and `Clock.elapsed`, which drives `delayedCall` timers and tween
progress, advances by that clamped delta. Under starvation (a few frames per
second) all game-time-paced choreography stretches: income phase gaps, coin
flights, the incident hold, and the deferral's own 250 ms `delayedCall`
re-polls. The deferral *deadline* (`s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`,
where `s.time.now` is the raw frame timestamp) is wall-clock, but it is only
re-checked at those clamped polls, so the forced day start is delayed by the
same starvation. Aggregate: closing choreography (stretched) + 16 s cap
(late-detected) + boot > the 40 s budget and the 60 s hook.

The cap's stated purpose is "end-of-turn can never hang the game"
(CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q, AC5/AC7). A stall bound that is only observed at frame
boundaries does not provide that guarantee — which is what this item fixes,
without touching the user-visible pacing.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer / gate runner** on the shared dev host: needs the browser
  gate green; a red `MainStreetScene` suite at ≈2× oversubscription burns whole
  sessions on retries and blocks the build → test → commit order.
- **Maintainer triaging a red browser suite**: needs a red wait to mean a
  behavioural regression, not host weather.
- **Release engineer** on the dev-push gate: a red gate on a loaded shared host
  stalls shipping even when the scene is correct.
- **Players**: unchanged pacing — the choreography, the incident hold and the
  cap value all stay as shipped; only the cap's *enforcement* becomes
  wall-clock rather than frame-clock, so under starvation the day advances at
  the documented bound instead of stalling past it.

Example user stories:

> As an agent running the browser gate on the shared 16-core host, I want the
> Enter-to-end-turn wait to pass at any load the host actually reaches, so that
> my gate result does not depend on which sibling suites happen to be running.

> As a player whose machine is momentarily overloaded, I want the end-of-turn
> to still advance within the documented safety window, so that the game can
> never appear hung.

## Existing state

- Measured envelope (2026-10-24, 16-core shared host): quiet 20/20 pass
  (peak 15.3); 8 burners 2/2 pass, then one fail at ambient 31.3; 16 burners
  fail at the 40 000 ms end-of-turn budget. Every other wait in the file passes
  at that load.
- The wait's effective budget is `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` (16 000) +
  `floorMs: END_TURN_STARVATION_MARGIN_MS` (24 000) = 40 000 ms, the largest
  that keeps the documented 20 000 ms scene-boot allowance inside the 60 s
  `testTimeout` (asserted by `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`). The
  suite's per-test timeout is already `it(..., 60_000)`.
- Five deferral polls race the choreography, all with the same shape
  (`startAt = <scene clock> + cap`, then `delayedCall(250, poll)`):
  3 in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`advanceTurn` ~433,
  forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) and 2 in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` (`finish`'s income wait
  ~254 and the reveal gating ~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` already has the
  degradation precedent: `scheduleOrRun` runs the callback immediately when the
  scene has no clock (headless), which a wall-clock helper must preserve.
- Node unit suites drive these polls through fake `time` stubs
  (`tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts`), and
  `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` pins "exactly three
  `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" by regex — both must be
  updated by the extraction.
- Reduced motion clears `incomeCollectionActive` synchronously in
  `MainStreetAnimatorIncome` (~line 1039), but it is **not** the remedy chosen:
  the parent rejected it as the sole remedy because it removes the
  deferred-income path from coverage.

## Desired change (decision: option C)

Replace the five duplicated deferral polls with **one shared, injectable
helper** that:

1. computes its deadline from a wall-clock timestamp (`Date.now()`),
2. re-polls with a wall-clock timer (`window.setTimeout`), not the scene clock,
3. forces completion (clearing `incomeCollectionActive` and invoking the
   caller's continuation) once `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time has
   elapsed since the deferral began,
4. is enforced even when the page is not painting — a backgrounded/hidden
   document ahead of the cap forces the advance rather than waiting for the
   next animation frame (Q2 = 1), and
5. degrades to today's behaviour where no clock/timer exists (headless node
   scenes run the continuation immediately), and exposes its clock/timer for
   deterministic unit driving.

Options considered and rejected (recorded for traceability):

- **A — accept and document the envelope** (no code change): the gate can still
  go red on the shared host when ambient load spikes ≥2×, conflicting with the
  "red tree never pushed" policy; rejected in favour of a root-cause fix.
- **B — reduced-motion Enter test + a separate cheap deferral-contract test**:
  no production change, but downgrades the file's end-to-end end-of-turn test
  to a synthetic and couples coverage to a reduced-motion implementation
  detail; retained only as a fallback if C's soak does not pass.
- **D — raise the browser hook for this test**: pure masking, requires
  amending the parent's "any derived budget must leave headroom for boot plus
  teardown within that hook" AC and re-baselining the guard's headroom rule,
  and would fail again at ≈4× oversubscription; rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **One bounded-deferral helper, wall-clock enforced.** All five
      income-collection deferral polls route through a single shared helper
      whose deadline is wall clock and whose re-poll is a wall timer; no inline
      `s.time.delayedCall(250, <poll>)` / `<scene clock> + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
      poll remains. A unit test with a frozen scene clock and an advancing wall
      clock proves the continuation is forced within one poll interval of the
      16 000 ms cap.
- [ ] **Forced advance is not tied to paint.** When the document is hidden / no
      frame runs, the cap still forces the advance after the cap elapses
      (Q2 = 1). A unit test asserts the wall timer — not the scene clock —
      drives the assertion, and the behaviour is documented in the module's
      code comment.
- [ ] **Injectable and backward-compatible.** The helper accepts an injectable
      clock/timer (so `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
      `turnflow.test.ts` and the new tests drive it deterministically) and
      preserves today's no-clock degradation (headless scenes run the
      continuation immediately).
- [ ] **Single source of truth for the cap.** `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` stays
      16 000 and remains the only cap value; the
      `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` "exactly three
      `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" pin is updated to the
      helper extraction (asserting the helper consumes the constant), so the
      duplication cannot silently return.
- [ ] **No production pacing change.** The choreography timing constants
      (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS`, flight/stagger durations, `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`)
      and the cap value are unchanged — pinned by existing/added unit tests;
      only the cap's enforcement mechanism differs.
- [ ] **Wait-budget guard still green.** `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`
      passes unchanged: the end-of-turn wait keeps its cap-derived 40 000 ms
      budget and `budget + 20 s boot ≤ 60 s` headroom rule. If the soak shows
      the budget can now be reduced, that reduction is a *derived* margin
      change proved by the soak, not a hand-picked literal.
- [ ] **Reliability proven, not assumed.** `/skill:test --type soak-load`
      (≥ `nproc` burners) passes with the change, and the pre-change failure at
      the same burner count is reproduced and recorded on this item; both
      before/after tables (burners, peak load, runs, wall times, summary paths)
      are posted as a comment.
- [ ] **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope" and
      the headroom rule section record the decision (cap enforced on wall
      clock, hidden-tab semantics) and the post-fix envelope, replacing the
      "above ~2× is outside the envelope" caveat with measured evidence; the
      helper's module comment documents the wall-clock contract. All related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
      README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes
      (`/skill:test --type full`), evidence recorded on this item.

## Constraints

- **No behavioural change to production pacing.** The choreography, the
  incident hold and the cap value are shipped features
  (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q); only the cap's enforcement may
  change.
- The parent's headroom constraint stands: `budget + scene-boot allowance` must
  stay inside the browser 60 s hook.
- Reduced motion must not become the sole remedy (parent decision); the
  deferred-income path keeps explicit coverage.
- All five deferral sites must keep identical semantics after extraction, and
  the existing fake-clock unit suites must not be weakened to accommodate the
  change.
- A stale wall timer must never fire into a destroyed scene — reuse the
  existing `scene.isActive()` / try-catch defensive pattern from the deferred
  closing tail.
- Agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill only
  (`/skill:test --type soak-load`, `--type full`); no ad-hoc `npx vitest` loops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` — add the shared
  wall-clock deferral helper (sibling to `scheduleOrRun` ~line 176); adopt it in
  `finish`'s income wait (~254) and the reveal gating (~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — three deferral sites
  (`advanceTurn` ~433, forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) adopt the
  helper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
  unchanged; comment updated to state the wall-clock enforcement contract.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` — the "exactly three
  `s.time.now + cap` sites" regex pin moves to the helper extraction.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — fake `time` stubs: drive the injected
  timer/clock.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — Enter test and its
  40 000 ms margin expected unchanged.
- `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` — headroom rule re-check (expected
  unchanged).
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — "Measured envelope" + headroom rule: record the
  decision and the post-fix soak evidence.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the clamped-delta mechanism is the dominant starvation link
  and the deferral's poll cadence is the part that can be fixed without touching
  pacing. Verified against the installed Phaser source
  (`TimeStep.smoothDelta`, `Clock.now` / `Clock.elapsed` semantics); the
  before/after `soak-load` run is the confirmation.
- **Risk:** removing the late-detection link may not be sufficient on its own —

# Wire Bank Loan button into the Turn Summary dialog

Follow-up raised by the Bank Loans planning session (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG), per producer
decision Q4: the Turn Summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) has landed, so its deliberately
disabled **Bank Loan** affordance can now be wired to the loan feature.

## Problem statement

The Turn Summary dialog shows an always-disabled **[ Bank Loan ]** button and never calls
the `onBankLoanAction` seam reserved for the loans feature, so a mid-game player has no
entry point to credit at all — the loan engine only surfaces offers on bankruptcy. This item
turns the reserved affordance into a working mid-game loan entry point, with no new engine
rules.

## Users

- **Mid-game human player (single-player)** — "When the Turn Summary dialog is on screen
  and I am short of cash, I want to borrow from the configured loan menu so I can fund the
  next week's move, and I want to see the repayment schedule before I commit."
- **Cautious player** — "I want the button to tell me *why* it is unavailable (loans turned
  off, or I already owe money) instead of a generic 'coming soon' note."

Not a user of this slice: competitive seats (per-seat closing text, no summary dialog),
AI seats (bailout-only policy — no proactive loans).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Enabled/disabled matrix.** The Bank Loan button is interactive only when
   `state.config.loansEnabled === true` **and** the acting (human) seat holds no active loan;
   in every other case it is rendered disabled (muted, `input` disabled) with a hint that
   explains the reason.
2. **Selector with schedule.** Pressing the enabled button opens the loan selector listing
   every configured `config.loanOptions` entry with its per-turn repayment and total
   repayment, plus a way to back out; backing out returns to the Turn Summary dialog with no
   state change.
3. **Confirm dispatches `takeLoan`.** Confirming an option dispatches the `takeLoan` command
   for the acting seat, credits the principal to that seat's wallet, records the active loan,
   and leaves `actionsRemaining` unchanged.
4. **No day advance.** Neither opening the selector nor confirming a loan advances the day or
   resumes the deferred closing; the day advances only on **[ Next Turn ]**, exactly once.
5. **Refreshed dialog.** After the loan is taken the Turn Summary dialog is re-rendered from
   the same `TurnResult` with the post-`takeLoan` state, so the new obligation is visible and
   the button is now disabled (one-active-loan rule) while **[ Next Turn ]** still works.
6. **Testing/validation.** Tests cover the enabled/disabled matrix (loans enabled + no loan,
   active loan, `loansEnabled: false`), the selector content, the `takeLoan` dispatch, the
   no-action-point rule, the cancel path, and that the day does not advance before
   **[ Next Turn ]**.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments (`showTurnSummaryDialog`, the gate, the button-construction site),
   `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (the "[ Bank Loan ] is always disabled" paragraph), and the
   in-game help/loan documentation touched by MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` renders `[ Bank Loan ]` with `disableInteractive()`, colour
  `#6b6459`, and the hint *“Bank loans are not available yet — coming in a future update.”*;
  it explicitly does `void onBankLoanAction` so the seam can never fire. `BANK_LOAN_HINT` is
  duplicated in `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`, whose AC4 asserts
  "always disabled, seam never invoked" — that test must be rewritten, not deleted.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` delegates to `msOverlayManager`; with no overlay manager (headless) it
  calls `onNextTurn()` immediately so the closing is never stranded.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `shouldGateTurnSummary()` restricts the
  dialog to `requiresDeferredClosing` single-player closings (never replay, reduced motion,
  tutorial or competitive); `presentTurnSummaryGate()` builds the summary with
  `buildTurnSummary(s.state, result)` and calls
  `s.showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn)` — the third argument is not passed today.
- Overlays already read live state (`s.state.config` in `MainStreetOverlayContent`), so
  `loansEnabled` needs no new plumbing into the scene.
- `buildTurnSummary()` is Phaser-free and read-only, so re-rendering after a loan only needs
  the same `state` + `result` pair re-run.
- **The loan engine has SHIPPED** (updated at plan time, 2026-11-01). The Bank Loans epic
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG and all 11 of its slices are `completed`, so the dependency edge is
  satisfied and this item is unblocked. Available to build on: `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`
  (`optionsFor`, `activeLoanFor`, `canTakeLoan`, `formatLoanObligation`,
  `buildActiveLoan`, `loanTotalRepayment`, `loanPerTurnRepayment`),
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` + `MainStreetLoanOverlayModel.ts` (bailout dialog),
  `takeLoan` / `acceptLoanOffer` in `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `takeLoanCommand` in
  `src/MainStreetCommands.ts`, and `config.loansEnabled` / `config.loanOptions`.
- **BLOCKER found at plan time: `canTakeLoan()` refuses the dialog's dispatch.**
  `canTakeLoan()` requires `state.phase === 'MarketPhase'`, but `presentTurnSummaryGate()`
  runs *before* `advanceTurn` → `finishDeferredTurnClosing()`, and `processEndOfTurn()` has
  already left the state in `IncidentPhase` (`MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:693`). A
  `takeLoan` dispatched from the dialog is therefore rejected with *"Loans can only be taken
  during the market phase, not IncidentPhase."* Producer decision **Q7 = A** (2026-11-01)
  authorises relaxing **only** the phase precondition for this window, which is why the
  original "presentation wiring only" constraint below is amended. Tracked by
  MS-0MVXYCIU00053HL1.
- **Repayment timing needs no change** (Assumption A1 now confirmed by code): the
  `LoanRepayment` pass runs inside the closing at `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:725`,
  before the dialog appears, so a loan taken at the dialog first repays on the *next* turn's
  closing automatically.
- Save schema v3 (loans + pending offer) is delivered by the epic; this slice must not touch
  serialisation.

## Desired change

1. **Carry a loans descriptor into the dialog.** Extend the gate's call so the dialog receives
   one small Phaser-free descriptor rather than reaching into scene state ad hoc — predicted
   shape `{ enabled: boolean; activeLoan: { perTurnRepayment, turnsRemaining } | null;
   options: LoanOption[] }` built in `presentTurnSummaryGate()` from `s.state.config` and the
   acting seat. Keeps the overlay presentation-only and the descriptor unit-testable.
   (Implementation may instead read `s.state` directly if the epic's helpers make that
   cleaner — the ACs do not care which; see Assumptions.)
2. **Enable the affordance** when `enabled && activeLoan === null`, wiring `pointerdown` to
   the `onBankLoanAction` seam; keep the button disabled otherwise with a reason-specific
   hint (loans disabled vs. already owing — see open question Q3).
3. **Loan selector** presented on press: reuse the epic's `MainStreetLoanOverlay` option rows
   (per-turn + total repayment). The epic builds it for a *pending offer* driven by
   `state.pendingLoanOffer`; this slice needs a non-bailout mode (no pending offer, options
   from `config.loanOptions`, Cancel/back instead of Decline). Reusing the row renderer, not
   duplicating it, is the requirement; a small `mode` parameter is expected.
4. **Confirm = dispatch.** Confirming dispatches the `takeLoan` command through the existing
   command surface (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`), never mutating state inline.
5. **Refresh in place** after a successful take: rebuild the summary from the same
   `TurnResult` and re-render the dialog (dismiss the old overlay objects first so
   `s.overlayObjects` stays consistent), leaving `[ Next Turn ]` as the only way to resume
   `advanceTurn`.
6. **Tests** in a new `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` (browser
   overlay, mirroring `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` helpers) plus the rewrite of the
   dialog suite's AC4 case.

## Constraints

- **Presentation wiring only, with one authorised exception (Q7 = A).** No changes to the
  loan model, repayment maths or the one-active-loan validation — those belong to
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG and stay untouched. The single permitted engine change is relaxing
  `canTakeLoan()`'s `MarketPhase` precondition for the seat's own deferred-closing window,
  behind an explicit opt-in, so the dialog's dispatch is not refused (see "Existing state").
- **No action point cost** and **no day advance** — taking a loan from the dialog must leave
  `actionsRemaining` untouched and must not resume the deferred closing.
- **Single-player deferred path only** — the dialog itself is gated to that path; competitive
  per-seat closing and the tutorial/reduced-motion/replay paths are unchanged.
- **Overlay conventions** (`core` UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` +
  `createOverlayButton`, all elements parented into `s.hudContainer` and pushed to
  `s.overlayObjects`, depths 199/200/201, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), SFX via
  `safePlaySound`.
- **Dependency now satisfied** — depended on MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (dependency edge already
  recorded): specifically the loan model/config slice (MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB), the `takeLoan`
  command slice (MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79) and the overlay-UI slice (MS-0MVPWSBLG006YMBA).

## Assumptions

- **A1 First repayment falls on the next turn's closing.** The closing sequence (and its
  ledger) has already run when the dialog is presented, so a loan taken at the dialog must not
  charge a repayment against the turn being summarised. **Confirmed at plan time by the
  shipped code** — the `LoanRepayment` pass runs inside the closing
  (`MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:725`) before the dialog is presented, so Q1 is resolved as
  A with no engine change.
- **A2 Proactive loans are allowed at any coin balance** — the button is not gated on
  affordability or negative coins (the goal is mid-game credit, not a second bailout path).
- **A3 The selector's rows come from `config.loanOptions`**, so a re-balanced menu needs no UI
  change, and the dialog is unavailable (button disabled) when the menu is empty.
- **A4 `takeLoan` rejection is surfaced, not swallowed** — if the engine refuses (e.g. a race
  into an active loan), the dialog shows the engine's reason and stays open rather than
  silently closing.
- **A5 Headless safety is untouched** — with no overlay manager the scene still calls
  `onNextTurn()`; the new descriptor must remain optional so existing call sites compile.

## Risks & mitigations

- **~~Sequencing risk (highest)~~ — RESOLVED at plan time:** the epic and all 11 slices are
  `completed`, so no engine helpers need inventing.
- **Phase-gate risk (now the highest):** `canTakeLoan()` refuses a take outside
  `MarketPhase`, but the dialog is presented during the deferred closing (`IncidentPhase`).
  Mitigation: producer Q7 = A authorises the narrow opt-in relaxation, isolated in
  MS-0MVXYCIU00053HL1 with explicit tests that every other refusal rule is unchanged.
- **Duplicated overlay logic:** copy-pasting the bailout overlay instead of parameterising it
  would leave two loan selectors to maintain. Mitigation: AC2/desired-change 3 require reusing
  the epic's row renderer.
- **Stale dialog content:** re-rendering from a mutated `state` but a stale `TurnResult` can
  show a mismatch. Mitigation: rebuild via `buildTurnSummary(state, result)` with the same
  `result` object (the ledger is presentation data, not recomputed).
- **Overlay object leak:** dismissing and re-rendering must reset `s.overlayObjects` the same
  way `dismissOverlay` does, or duplicated buttons accumulate in `hudContainer`. Mitigation:
  explicit test asserting a single `[ Next Turn ]`/`[ Bank Loan ]` pair after a refresh.
- **Test drift:** `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` AC4 encodes "always disabled"; leaving
  it untouched makes the suite self-contradictory. Mitigation: rewrite that case in the same
  commit.
- **Scope creep:** competitive-mode parity (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI), AI proactive loans, multiple
  loans, loan repayment UI polish — record as linked work items, do not fold in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — enable/disable `[ Bank Loan ]`, wire the seam,
  render the reason-specific hint and refresh the dialog after a take.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — build and pass the loans descriptor in
  `presentTurnSummaryGate()`; keep `shouldGateTurnSummary()` unchanged.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — pass the descriptor through the delegation method.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — reuse the epic's option rows in a non-bailout
  (mid-game select) mode.
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — consume `activeLoanFor` / option-table helpers (read-only use).
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoan` command dispatch and the no-AP assertion.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` — **new.** Wiring tests.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` — rewrite the "seam never invoked"
  case.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — update the "always disabled" Turn Summary paragraph.

## Out of scope / non-goals

- Competitive-mode summary dialog and any competitive loan entry point
  (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI).
- Engine rules: repayment timing, bailout offer loop, AI policy, persistence — owned by
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG.
- HUD obligation readout (MS-0MVPWSCRD004A6Z4) and the loans help/documentation slice
  (MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB); this item only edits the one doc paragraph it invalidates.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** (Bank Loans, epic, `intake_complete`) — the engine this slice wires
  into; dependency edge recorded.
- **MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB** (Loan model, config and repayment maths), **MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79**
  (`takeLoan` command and one-active-loan rule), **MS-0MVPWSBLG006YMBA** (Bailout overlay UI
  and deferred closing resume) — prerequisites.
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (End of Turn summary, completed) — parent of the dialog; its AC
  anticipated the Bank Loan button.
- **MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT** (Overlay: turn summary dialog + browser test, completed) — created
  the disabled affordance and its `onBankLoanAction` seam.
- **MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R** (deferred closing gate, completed) — the gate that presents the
  dialog; see `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Turn Summary dialog and the closing gate".
- **MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI** (End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode, open) — the other
  mode's dialog; explicitly not covered here.
- Repo: `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`,
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (repayment timing): "A loan taken from the Turn Summary dialog — when does the first
  repayment hit? (A) at the next turn's closing, since this turn's closing and ledger have
  already run [recommended]; (B) immediately when the deferred closing resumes, so the turn
  just summarised carries it; (C) other." — **Answer (resolved at plan time by code, not
  producer): A.** The `LoanRepayment` pass runs inside the closing
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:725`) before the summary dialog appears, so a loan
  taken at the dialog first repays on the next turn's closing automatically — no engine change
  needed. Evidence: `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, `applyLoanRepayments` call site.
  Final: A.
- Q2 (mode scope): "Should the enabled button also cover any non-single-player summary
  surface? (A) no — single-player deferred path only; competitive parity stays with
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI [recommended]; (B) cover competitive too." — **Answer (resolved at
  plan time by code): A.** `shouldGateTurnSummary()` returns false for every competitive
  closing, so the dialog (and thus the button) can only ever appear on the single-player
  deferred path. Final: A.
- Q3 (disabled hint wording): "When the seat already holds an active loan, what should the
  disabled hint say? (A) show the outstanding obligation, e.g. *'Active loan: 110 coins/week,
  4 weeks left.'* [recommended]; (B) a generic *'You already have an active loan.'*; (C) keep
  the current generic text." — **Answer (producer, interactive plan session 2026-11-01):
  A** — show the outstanding obligation, built from `formatLoanObligation()` so the wording
  matches the HUD readout (e.g. `Loan: 110 coins/turn, 4 turns left`). This is also how AC5's
  "the new obligation is visible" is satisfied, because `buildTurnSummary()` carries no loan
  fields. Final: A.
- Q4 (proactive eligibility): "Is the button available at any balance, or only when the seat
  cannot cover its costs?" — answered from the seed goal (mid-game credit use case): **any
  balance**, recorded as Assumption A2. Source: work-item description "As a mid-game player …
  I can click [ Bank Loan ]".
- Q5 (selector reuse): "Does the epic's bailout overlay support a non-bailout option list?" —
  research: `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` does not exist yet; the epic's Key Files
  predict it as the pending-offer overlay. Draft therefore requires a reuse with a mode
  parameter rather than a copy (Risks: duplicated overlay logic). Source: `wl show

- Q6 (dependency): "Is the loan engine available to wire against?" — research: no — `grep -ri
  loan src` returns only the dialog's placeholder comments; the epic is at `intake_complete`

  loan --json`.

  deferred closing when the phase is `IncidentPhase` (`MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:693`),

## Goal

Harden the competitive Turn Summary end-to-end: only the seats the closing
actually surfaced get rows, every non-competitive and non-interactive path keeps
today's pacing byte-for-byte, and the gate provably adds no save, no state

1. Eliminated seats produce no row (no ghost rows): the panel renders exactly the seats the closing surfaced, and a test asserts row-count and row-identity against an engine run with one eliminated seat.

# Per-turn stat history capture and series model

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (tracer bullet, phase 1).

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want my run's per-turn economy recorded and the
final **Cash at end of turn** shown in the Game Over Summary, so the run's
trajectory survives the run and can be charted in the next phase.

## Scope

- **In:** `TurnStatSnapshot` type + `turnStatsHistory` initialisation, capture
  on **every** end-of-turn closing path, save/load persistence with a legacy
  `[]` fallback, the pure `buildGameOverStatSeries` model, and the Summary
  column's cash-at-end-of-turn line.
- **Out:** graph/chart rendering (third-column child), competitive-mode series
  assertions, prose documentation (docs child). Inline JSDoc only here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn on the legacy and deferred paths, never twice.
2. **Snapshot shape and capture.** `TurnStatSnapshot { turn, coins,
   reputation, score, profit, businesses, staff }` is exported from
   `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`, and `turnStatsHistory` is added to
   `MainStreetState` and initialised to `[]` by both `setupMainStreetGame` and
   `createCompetitiveState`; `profit = coins − (weekStartCoins ?? current
   coins)` (the `appendTurnNetRow` definition), `businesses` = non-null
   `streetGrid` entries, `staff = staffCards.length`. Capture lives in the
   shared closing tail so the legacy path (`runSinglePlayerTurnClosing`,
   including its immediate-loss early exit), the deferred path
   (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, including its immediate-loss early exit) and
   the competitive closing path each record exactly once; a repeat call for the
   same `turn` appends nothing; `npm run build` (tsc) is clean.
3. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState`.
4. **Persistence details.** It is restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`; a
   legacy save without the field loads with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data). Unit tests cover round-trip fidelity and the legacy
   fallback.
5. **Pure series model.** `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)` in
   `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` returns the five series
   (profit, cash, businesses, staff, reputation at end of turn) as labelled
   point arrays plus `finalCash` (last recorded `coins`, falling back to
   `state.resourceBank.coins` for an empty history). No Phaser import; an empty
   history yields empty series and a valid `finalCash`. Unit tests cover a
   populated history, an empty history, and non-mutation of `state`.
6. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture on both paths and no
   double-record.
7. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established overlay
   conventions: `hudContainer` parenting, depth 201 and `overlayObjects`.
8. **Summary cash line.** `showGameOverOverlay` renders
   `Cash at end of turn: <n>` in the Summary column directly after the score
   breakdown, with no clipping and no change to existing Summary content, and
   reads committed state only (the snapshot is byte-identical before/after the
   call); an overlay unit test asserts the line renders and the existing
   content is retained.

## Minimal implementation

1. `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory` on
   `MainStreetState` and `MainStreetSerializedState`.
2. `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — `turnStatsHistory: []` in both setups.
3. `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — record from the shared closing tail
   (`appendTurnNetRow`) via a small `recordTurnStats(state, turnEnded)` helper,
   keyed by `turn`.
4. `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialise the array; restore with
   `saved.turnStatsHistory ?? []` (tolerate malformed entries defensively).
5. `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — `buildGameOverStatSeries`.
6. `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Summary cash line.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — snapshot interface + state/serialized fields.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — initialise `turnStatsHistory: []`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `recordTurnStats` called from the
  closing tail.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialise/restore with legacy fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — `buildGameOverStatSeries`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Summary cash line.
- `tests/main-street/turn-stats-history.test.ts` — **new** capture/persistence
  unit tests.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stat-series.test.ts` — **new** series-model
  unit tests.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` — extended cash-line assertion.

## Dependencies

None. Blocks the chart, third-column, competitive, docs and acceptance children.

## Deliverables

Code + unit tests + inline JSDoc, all green under the changed-scope test gate.

## Risks

- Deferred and legacy closing paths may record twice — mitigated by the
  `turn`-keyed guard and targeted tests.
- Competitive closing reuses the shared scratch bank; this child records what
  the closing tail sees and defers the seat-scope assertion to the competitive
  child.

# Chart library integration spike

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 2, risk burn-down).

## Goal (user story)

As a developer on Main Street, I want proven, isolated Chart.js integration
with the Phaser 4 canvas so the end-of-game graphs can be built on a known-good
foundation instead of during layout work.

## Context

Producer decision Q3 = **B**: use an external charting library (e.g. Chart.js)
rather than hand-rolled `Graphics` or SVG-as-texture. Chart.js needs a canvas
context and a DOM element, and it must never load or run in replay / headless
(Monte-Carlo) runs. This spike de-risks that integration before five graphs are
laid out.

## Scope

- **In:** dependency addition, a thin `MainStreetStatsChart.ts` wrapper, one
  working overlay chart, headless/replay skip, teardown, bundle-size evidence
  and a documented spike verdict.
- **Out:** the five real graphs and column layout (third-column child), styling
  polish, docs prose (docs child).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dependency.** The chosen charting library (Chart.js preferred) is added to
   `dependencies` in `package.json` with the lockfile updated; `npm run build`
   is clean; the production bundle-size delta (before/after, kB and gzip) is
   recorded in a work-item comment.
2. **Wrapper exists and is Phaser-thin.** `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts`
   exposes a create/destroy pair (e.g. `createStatsChart(scene, geometry, spec)`
   → handle, `destroyStatsChart(handle)`) that renders **one line chart** into a
   dedicated DOM `<canvas>` positioned over the Phaser canvas at the requested
   overlay coordinates; the module has no game-state imports and no Phaser
   scene mutation.
3. **Headless/replay safe.** `createStatsChart` returns `null` and creates no
   DOM node when `scene.replayMode` is true or when no DOM is available
   (`typeof document === 'undefined'`); a unit test with a mocked chart
   constructor asserts zero constructions and zero nodes in both cases.
4. **Lazy-loaded.** The library is imported via a dynamic `import()` from the
   overlay path so headless/Monte-Carlo/replay entry points never resolve it;
   the existing engine/headless unit tests pass unchanged (changed-scope gate).
5. **No animation, clean teardown.** Charts are created with
   `animation: false` and no rAF/tween loop (reduced-motion safe); destroying
   the overlay removes every chart canvas — a browser test opens and closes the
   overlay 20 times and asserts zero leftover chart canvases and no console
   errors.
6. **Verdict recorded.** A work-item comment states: library + version, bundle
   delta, layering/positioning approach, teardown evidence, and whether the
   spike meets its thresholds (chart visible above the overlay panel at
   1280×720; gzip delta ≤ 150 kB; no leaks). If a threshold fails, the comment
   records the alternative approach and the item stops for producer review
   instead of continuing to the third-column child.

## Minimal implementation

1. `package.json` — add the charting dependency.
2. `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — dynamic-import wrapper, skip guards,
   positioning over the Phaser canvas, `destroyStatsChart` teardown.
3. Temporary wiring in `showGameOverOverlay` to draw one series so the browser
   test can exercise the real path.
4. Tests: unit skip/no-leak test with a mocked library, browser open/close
   cycle test.
5. Bundle measurement + spike comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — charting dependency.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **new** wrapper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — temporary single-chart wiring.
- `tests/main-street/stats-chart.test.ts` — **new** unit skip/no-leak tests.
- `tests/main-street/stats-chart.browser.test.ts` — **new** browser teardown
  test.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the capture/series-model child (needs `buildGameOverStatSeries`).
Blocks the third-column child.

## Deliverables

Dependency + wrapper + tests + spike verdict comment.

## Risks

- Chart.js may fight the Phaser canvas for pointer/depth ordering — the wrapper
  must own a separate DOM layer and stay non-interactive in this phase.

   links the stats column.

   focuses the stats column without animation (static focus frame and/or depth

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 4).

## Goal (user story)

As a competitive Main Street player, I want the same end-of-game graphs for my
own seat so a loss against the AI can be diagnosed, and I want the overlay to
fit the viewport in both game modes.

## Scope

- **In:** competitive-series scope, both-mode rendering/fit verification,
  replay/headless guard verification, reduced-motion confirmation.
- **Out:** per-seat multi-series graphs (only if the producer overrides the
  recorded working assumption — that would be a separate item), docs prose.

## Working assumption (plan Open Question)

Competitive mode plots the **human seat's** trajectory only (see the parent's
Appendix "OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope)"). This child asserts
and documents that assumption; it must not expand to per-seat series without
producer confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Competitive series.** With a competitive fixture (`players[]` populated),
   the rendered series equal the recorded `turnStatsHistory` for the human
   seat's closing values, and no AI seat's wallet leaks into the series (unit
   test asserting series points against a hand-built competitive history).
2. **Human-seat recording.** The competitive closing path records one history
   entry per turn from the seat-scoped closing wallet (`findHumanSeatId`

## Problem

While finishing MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O the dev push ran **no** git hook:

- `git config --get core.hooksPath` → unset
- `.git/hooks/pre-push` → absent (only `post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite` plus `.sample` files)
- the repo's `.githooks/pre-push` exists but is never invoked from this checkout.

Consequences (the documented dev-push integration gates are inert here):

1. **No full-suite gate on dev pushes** — the framework documents the pre-push hook as the deterministic full-suite integration gate (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81); here a red tree can be pushed straight to `dev`. Note this repo's `.githooks/pre-push` in fact only enforces branch policy + context budget + worklog sync — it has no test-suite step at all — so even when wired it would not provide the documented gate.
2. **No protected-branch check** — a regular agent could push to `main`/`master` without the hook's refusal.
3. **No worklog auto-sync on push**.

## Why it matters

Agent push discipline (push only to `dev`, green suite before push, worklog sync) is currently enforced only by agent behaviour, not by the repository. Any audit that assumes "the hook ran the full suite" is relying on something that did not happen.

## Investigation starting points

- How hooks are installed (framework install script and `.githooks/` → `.git/hooks/` wiring) and why `pre-push` is missing here while `post-*` hooks are present.
- Whether `core.hooksPath` should be `.githooks` per clone (and re-set after a fresh clone/worktree).
- Whether `.githooks/pre-push` should gain the `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` step the framework docs describe.

## Out of scope

Fixing anything about MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O — that item is complete and its evidence came from an explicit `/skill:test` full-scope run.

# Goal

As a maintainer, I want the Help/Settings **browser** tests to fail when the
panels stop rendering, so a pixel regression cannot slip through a soft check.

Discovered during `MS-0MVU03UEC000BX1O` (WebGL clipping test hardening): the two
Canvas-mode panel tests listed below carry assertions that can never fail, which
is exactly the class of low-value test the shared Test Writing Guidelines
forbid (anti-pattern 2 — "Placeholder Tests": always-pass, zero-effect
assertions).

## Scope

- `tests/main-street/HelpSettingsButtons.browser.test.ts`
  - `expect(hudHasHelp || true).toBeTruthy()` / `expect(hudHasSettings || true).toBeTruthy()`
    — always true (guideline anti-pattern 2: zero-effect assertions).
  - Duplicated `expect(hl).toBeDefined()` / `expect(sl).toBeDefined()` re-checks
    that repeat earlier assertions.
  - The panel pixel probe tolerates a 180 colour-distance delta, which is wider
    than the distance between the panel background and several scene colours.
- `tests/main-street/HelpPanelLayering.browser.test.ts`
  - The Settings-panel pixel checks are downgraded to `console.warn()` (never
    assertions) when they are weak.
  - Both tests fall back to a logical-only assertion when
    `panelContainer.x` has not moved, so neither test proves the panel is
    actually painted in CI (`waitForScene` + headless tweens do advance — the
    WebGL probes in `webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` rely on it).
  - The Settings guard `if (panelContainer.x <= canvas.width)` is true both when
    the panel is open (`canvasWidth - panelWidth`) and closed (`canvasWidth`),
    so that test can never reach its assertion branch.
  - The Settings panel colour is hardcoded as `0x101020` (16,16,32), but
    `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` paints `PANEL_BG_COLOR = 0x1a1a2e`
    (26,26,46) — the expected colour must come from the panel's own constant.
  - Debug `console.info()` calls left in the test body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every assertion in both files can fail: no `|| true`, no assertion-free
  branches, no `console.warn()` in place of an `expect`, and no duplicated
  existence re-checks.
- Panel pixels are probed through `renderer.snapshotPixel()` with rects derived
  from the panels' own layout constants (`HelpPanel`/`SettingsPanel`
  `panelWidth`, container `x`/`y`, background rect geometry) — same helper
  pattern as `webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts`. Expected panel colours
  are read from each panel's own `PANEL_BG_COLOR` constant, never a hardcoded
  literal.
- Numeric thresholds are named constants documented as narrower than the
  measured panel-vs-scene colour distance, so a scene-only frame cannot satisfy
  them.
- Each test proves paint, not just state: an inside-rect probe matches the
  panel colour **and** an outside-rect probe does not, so removing the panel's
  rendering fails the test.
- Both tests stay on `Phaser.CANVAS` (CI speed) and pass in the browser
  project. Canvas-mode `snapshotPixel()` is available in the pinned Phaser 4
  renderer (`node_modules/phaser/src/renderer/canvas/CanvasRenderer.js`), so no
  WebGL boot is required.
- The `webgl-clipping-browser` group / `.pi/test-config.json` entry is updated
  (or a group declared) so the changed-scope gate runs both files.

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/HelpSettingsButtons.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/HelpPanelLayering.browser.test.ts`
- `core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`
- `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`
- `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` (helper pattern reference)
- `.pi/test-config.json`

## Related

- `MS-0MVU03UEC000BX1O` — Harden WebGL clipping test: zero exclusions (the
  sibling hardening item this work was discovered during).

## Open Questions

- **OPEN QUESTION** (maintainers): should the pixel-probe helpers be extracted
  into a shared test helper (e.g. `tests/main-street/helpers/panelPixelProbe.ts`)
  alongside the existing `helpers/panelTreatment.ts`, or kept local to the two
  files? The item does not decide this; either is acceptable provided the ACs

# Bank loan offer: show the shortfall needed to reach the next turn

## Problem statement

The bankruptcy bailout dialog (titled **Bank Loan Offer**) tells a player only
*"You cannot cover this turn's costs."* It never names the amount, so the player
cannot see how far short they are, cannot judge whether any offered loan is big
enough, and — in the case where even the largest option leaves them negative —
gets no warning at all before committing to debt that will not save the run.

## Users

- **Human player facing bankruptcy (single- and competitive mode)** — "When the
  Bank Loan Offer appears I want it to say how much cash I am short, so I know
  what has to be borrowed to reach the next turn."
- **Cost-conscious player** — "I want each loan option to tell me whether it
  actually covers the gap, so I do not borrow €300 when I am €800 short — or
  borrow more than I need because I had to do the arithmetic myself."
- **Player reading back the activity log** — "I want the bailout log row to state
  the shortfall in coins, not a raw negative balance I have to interpret."

Not a user of this item: AI/headless seats (they auto-accept the largest option
and never see the dialog) and mid-game borrowers (the Turn Summary loan selector,
MS-0MVPWSQMG004198C — see Non-goals).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The offer states the amount.** While a bankruptcy bailout offer is open, the
   dialog states the exact amount of coins needed to reach the next turn, in the
   game's currency formatting (e.g. *"You are €80 short of covering this turn's
   costs."*), in place of the current amount-free sentence.
2. **The amount is the closing deficit.** The stated figure is the shortfall that
   triggered the offer: `max(0, −coins)` evaluated on the same balance the
   bankruptcy test used — the shared wallet in single-player, the seat's
   `PlayerRecord.coins` in competitive mode, and the **projected** closing balance
   on the deferred-mutation path — never a fresh re-read at render time. It
   excludes the loan's first instalment, which is charged on the next turn
   (docs §5.1, "First instalment timing"), and is a whole, non-negative coin
   amount.
3. **Per-option coverage.** Every option row states whether that loan closes the
   gap: rows that do state it closes the gap, and rows that do not state how many
   coins the seat would still be short after taking it (e.g. *"[ Borrow €300 —
   €110/turn, €330 total over 3 turns — €20 short ]"*). When **no** presented
   option closes the gap, the dialog additionally warns that any of these loans
   still leaves the seat below zero and the run will end.
4. **Log row agrees.** The activity-log row written when the offer is raised
   states the shortfall in coins (replacing the raw `coins are -80` phrasing) so
   the log and the dialog cannot disagree.
5. **Persistence.** The shortfall travels with the pending offer across a
   save/load round-trip, so a save taken mid-offer restores the same figure. A
   v3 (or v2) save whose pending offer carries no shortfall loads and behaves
   exactly as today — the offer is still resolvable and the figure is shown as
   unknown rather than being invented. **No save schema version bump** is
   required (the field is additive and optional inside the existing
   `pendingLoanOffer`).
6. **No behaviour change.** Offer-raising rules, the one-offer-per-seat-per-turn
   guard, the AI/headless largest-option policy, the loan menu, the repayment
   maths and the bankruptcy outcome are all unchanged; loans-off headless
   closings remain byte-identical (golden baseline still passes).
7. **Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the shortfall computation
   (single-player, competitive seat, deferred projected balance, and the
   guard that a non-negative balance never raises an offer), the dialog model
   (intro text, per-row coverage flags, the no-option-covers warning, the
   back-compatible unknown-shortfall path), the save/load round-trip, and the
   rendered dialog text in the browser overlay suite.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
   §5.1 (bailout bullet: the offer states the shortfall and each option's
   coverage), and the in-game help content where the bailout is described.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only change to the offer.** No new engine rules, no change to
  when an offer is raised, which option the AI accepts, or what happens on
  accept/decline. The only state change is one extra field on the pending offer.
- **Snapshot, not recomputation.** The deficit must be captured when the offer is
  raised (`state.pendingLoanOffer`), because on the deferred-mutation path the
  turn's deltas are still un-applied when the dialog renders; recomputing from
  the live wallet in the model would show a wrong (post-pause) figure for a
  competitive seat or a deferred single-player closing.
- **Integer economy, integer copy.** Coins are integers (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6); the
  figure is rounded/floored to a whole coin and never rendered as a fraction.
- **Overlay conventions.** Any new text uses the existing overlay patterns in
  `MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` (depths 199/200/201, elements parented into
  `hudContainer`, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance), and the
  dialog content is produced by the Phaser-free
  `buildLoanOfferModel()` so it stays unit-testable.
- **No scope creep into the Turn Summary item.** The mid-game selector in
  MS-0MVPWSQMG004198C is in flight; this item must not modify it or block on it.

## Existing state
